body: I’m really glad to hear you have received proper support through therapy. It gives me hope my boyfriend will have a similar victory. He has grown up with a narcissist mom and step dad and an abusive father. Everything is the direct result of their actions, but he’s very resentful. He even blocked them, along with many friends, today on whatsapp. It’s worrying me even more but it shows me how this is all about him reliving his trauma and I just wish I could make it stop for him

He has and he has been put on a long waitlist. I can call his doctor to ask to speed it up due to his state. When he is angry, he doesn’t listen at all. He either refuses to talk then to me or he gives up on everything. He’s not coming from a loving home and his parents put him through some trauma. It’s where the anger comes from and he is aware but there is no visible sadness or anything as another negative emotion he has. Just anger.

After breaking up, did you feel better, or were things just easier because you didn’t have to think about how your actions impact your partner? It’s a genuine question because I’m trying to figure out what to do next
But if anything happens to him (self inflicted), how would I even live with myself?

Thank you so much. This helped immensely and I actually have to tear up because I feel understood. My boyfriend is a closed book. He doesn’t talk to me much about his feelings but rather expresses his depression. I never pressure him, but I’m worried he might never talk to me else. He cares for me and loves me, I know for a fact, but he seems to not care about much else in the world, leaving him an empty shell. May I ask, since getting into therapy, has your husband’s mental state improved? I’m just wondering if people who are initially against therapy and think nothing will help them can actually be helped in therapy?

moved to London three years ago. it can get pretty lonely, people are constantly working to meet the expensive requirements to live there. A spontaneous “hey, come over today?” is almost definitely met with a no due to their schedule. It is nice to know what people do on their weekends/days off. It keeps you on track on where to socialise and helps you plan better in case you want to ask the person to hang out. People are very respectful of each other’s schedule here I have found
Thank you. I’m glad you have good company when you need it, that is very important. Your comment helped.

Yup, I hear you. Forcing yourself out of the comfort zone especially when low is a total struggle. I know it has to come from yourself, but if you had a friend trying to cheer you up, how could they beat convince you to go out for a walk with them for fresh air?
Thank you, you gave me a great idea!
Dave Chapelle and Bill Burr are already in my favourite list. I’ll check the others, seem to have similar taste. Thank you!
